newsitem.title: INDIA: No decision seen on India's MAT tax before budget.
newsitem.headline: No decision seen on India's MAT tax before budget.

text.p: The Indian government is unlikely to announce any decision on the minimum alternate tax (MAT) on companies until it presents the 1997/98 (April-March) budget next month, Finance Ministry officials said on Tuesday.
"I don't think we are going to announce anything on the MAT separately from the budget," said a ministry official who asked not to be named. "On MAT, I don't think you should expect anything now."
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram is expected to present the 1997/98 budget to parliament on February 28, the official said.

The official said the government was not expected to announce a single package of measures this month to bolster industrial growth and boost capital markets. Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda has promised to take such steps this month.

"Measures will be announced in bits and pieces," the Finance Ministry official said. "There will not be a one-time announcement, but rather a whole series of announcements, some of which have already been made."

The official cited a recent decision to grant a tax exemption for long-term capital gains earned on shares issued by publicly traded firms engaged in infrastructure development as one of a series of measures which have already been announced.
Business leaders and bourse executives have called on the government to scrap the MAT, which was introduced in the 1996/97 budget presented by Chidambaram last July.
Under the MAT, an effective minimum tax rate of 12.9 percent is levied on companies which had previously been exempt from corporate tax by showing fresh capital expenditure.
Industrialists say the tax has hit corporate profits, undermining share prices.

But senior economists who met Chidambaram last week as part of a series of pre-budget meetings with the finance minister defended the MAT, saying it should be retained or replaced with an alternative.
"There really is mixed opinion on this," the Finance Ministry official said. "I'm not very sure what turn this will take."
Last month Deve Gowda told businessmen he would consider their complaints against the MAT before the presentation of the 1997/98 budget.

There has been speculation that the government might make an announcement relating to the MAT as part of measures which Deve Gowda has promised to take this month to strengthen industrial production and boost capital markets.
Last week Chidambaram was quoted as saying he would take a decision soon on the MAT.

Any measures to bolster the capital markets would probably be announced before Deve Gowda and Chidambaram leave to attend the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, later this month, the Finance Ministry official said.
The exact date of their anticipated departure was not yet known, but the official said they were expected to leave on January 27 or 28.
